title: Tor-independent base change for perfect derived coinduction
statement:
Let $A\to B$ and $A\to A'$ be maps of commutative rings, set $B'=B\otimes_AA'$, assume $B[0]$ is a perfect $A$-complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and assume $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(B,A')=0$ for every $i>0$. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and derived coinduction $C_B^A$ [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. For every $N\in D(A)$ the evaluation-counit mate is an isomorphism in $D(B')$:
$$C_B^A(N)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{B'}^{A'}(N\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A').$$
Its underlying $A'$-map is the perfect derived-Hom base-change map [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], using $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B'$. The comparisons preserve evaluation counits, are natural in $N$, and commute with identity and successive Tor-independent scalar extensions. In particular they commute with polynomial Koszul evaluation maps and their ordered tensor signs whenever those maps are scalar-extended. No Noetherianity or flatness of $A\to A'$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), case (1), 0661 (lemma-base-change-comparison), and 07VI (lemma-dual-perfect-complex); B-action and counit enhancement by dualizing.tex Tags 0A70 and 0A71.

proof.text: Choose a free resolution $F^\bullet\to B[0]$, in nonpositive cochain degrees. Its terms are flat, so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes it K-flat. By the resolution definition [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], $H^{-i}(F\otimes_A A')=\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(B,A')$ for $i\geq0$. Positive cohomology is zero and $H^0=B'$. Thus the augmentation $F\otimes_A A'\to B'[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This gives the canonical identification $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\simeq B'[0]$, exactly the Tor-independence hypothesis in the exchange node.

source.place: Tag 0661 (lemma-base-change-comparison), resolution argument; bounded-flat input Tag 064K.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange] with its $(P,A,T,A_T)=(A,B,A',B')$ and $M=N$. The previous step verifies its derived Tor-independence hypothesis, and perfectness is precisely the present assumption on $B[0]$. Write $U,U'$ for the two restriction functors. The exchange node supplies $\theta_X:U'(X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B')\simeq UX\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'$ and an isomorphism $\gamma_N$ in $D(B')$. Its defining adjunct is $(\epsilon_N\otimes1)\theta_{C_B^A(N)}$, so it is the evaluation-counit mate required here, with its actual $B'$-action, rather than merely an isomorphism of underlying objects. In particular $\epsilon'_{N\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'}U'(\gamma_N)=(\epsilon_N\otimes1)\theta_{C_B^A(N)}$ by the adjunction [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction].

Identify the underlying map, including its normalization. The coinduction adjunction [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] sends a map $g:UX\to N$ to the map with value $x\mapsto(b\mapsto g(bx))$; its inverse evaluates at $1$. Consequently the scalar-extended counit of step 2, evaluated at $b\otimes t\in B'$, gives the Hom comparison $h\otimes a'\mapsto(b\otimes t\mapsto a't(h(b)\otimes1))$. This is exactly the scalar-extension formula defining the canonical Hom base-change map [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. To interpret the formula on arbitrary derived $N$, use that definition's bounded finite-projective representative $P$ of $B[0]$, K-flat representative $Q$ of $N$, and canonical K-injective comparison: in every Hom coordinate the same formula is $(h\otimes a')(x\otimes t)=a't(h(x)\otimes1)$. Both constructions insert these comparison maps, so they give the same localized morphism, not just the same cohomology maps. Tensor symmetry changes between the left-scalar convention of that definition and our right-scalar convention; scalars have degree zero. Thus, under $\theta$ and step 1, $U'(\gamma_N)$ is the canonical perfect derived-Hom base-change isomorphism of [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect], applied to $(E,K)=(B[0],N)$.

source.place: Tag 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), equation-base-change-RHom and case (1); dualizing.tex Tags 0A70 and 0A71.

proof.text: Naturality and the equality of direct and successive comparisons are supplied by [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange]. The counit equation in step 2 specifies their counit compatibility. For the identity extension, $\theta$ is the unit identification and the defining adjunct is $\epsilon_N$; the adjunction bijection [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] therefore makes $\gamma_N$ the identity. For a tower $A\to A'\to A''$, apply the exchange node when the indicated squares are Tor independent; after the canonical associators its direct and successive maps agree. There is no additional choice of an automorphism of coinduction, since each comparison was specified as a counit mate.

source.place: Tag 0661 (lemma-base-change-comparison), canonical comparisons; dualizing.tex Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint); agent adjunction-bijection calculation.

proof.text: Finally consider any polynomial Koszul evaluation map that is scalar-extended as in the statement. A finite Koszul complex has terms finite exterior powers of a finite free module, hence is a bounded finite-free complex. Apply the dual comparison of [lem-pod-perfect-dual-scalar-calculus] to that complex. For homogeneous $x,\phi$ of degrees $p,j$, signed evaluation after extension has value $(-1)^{pj}\iota(\phi(x))ab$ on $(x\otimes b)\otimes(\phi\otimes a)$, exactly its asserted scalar-extended evaluation. For an ordered tensor of such factors the interchange sign is the product of the corresponding $(-1)^{pj}$; a ring map preserves each sign and the chosen order. Step 3 identifies this Hom scalar map with our comparison; thus the scalar-extended Koszul evaluations commute with it, with precisely these signs. This uses only the scalar extension of the specified maps, and imposes no assertion that a nonregular Koszul complex resolves its quotient.

source.place: Tag 07VI (lemma-dual-perfect-complex) and section-sign-rules; agent specialization of the explicit scalar-dual evaluation formula.
